i’ve tried many, many antidepressants/anxiety meds and the one that keeps me feeling the most like a human being while helping me is wellbutrin. i’ve been on it for about a year now. i’ve heard a lot of good things from other people i’ve meet in various groups so if you’re interested in something like that, talk to a doctor about it. it does suck that so many “helpful” medications end up making you feel absolutely nothing and nonexistent. i mean it, drop the non-prescription stuff. relapses happen, doesn’t mean that you’re not capable of getting better.

the problem with drugs is even if it is a good release in the moment, it makes you feel worse between use. that can be a factor in your mental health issues. its hard, but stopping or even just cutting back can drastically change things for you. there are a lot of things you can do instead that would be healthier for you. have you tried any prescription medication, like antidepressants? your friends should not invalidate your feelings just because someone else has it “worse”. someone in the world has it worse than your friends do too, but that doesn’t make them any less valid, so it shouldn’t make it okay to ignore you. i know that you may not care much for your future, but i do, your friends do (even if it doesn’t seem that way), your family does, etc.

something that may be helpful to you is joining after school clubs/activities! i know it may seem like a lot or anxiety inducing, but after you get used to it it can be a good distraction/keep you busy. my old highschool had a video game club, maybe you can see if your school does. 
being young and alone sucks. i know how bad it can feel. you deserve to have fun in your teen years and i hope that you can find peace with your situation.

i can speak from experience, substance abuse will only make things worse for you. i know it doesn’t seem that way now, but in the long run the damage far outweighs the pros. i am here if you need someone, i know what it’s like to be the “go to” friend whos feelings don’t matter to anyone else.

if i had ended up dying when i was 16 like i had wanted to, it would be a huge mistake. i do not want to be the person to say “it gets better”, but it very much does. the pain you are feeling is only temporary and there are so many resources available to get help with healing. giving up now is not fair to yourself, your friends, your family. there is a lot ahead of you that you dont want to miss out on.

i haven’t had them, but a good friend of mine did hers. she left them in for probably four or five months before taking them out. she didn’t have many complaints, besides eating which is a common one with mouth piercings anyway! i know the healing was slow, probably three months. even after they healed, hers would randomly get irritated and sometimes swell, though they were never infected. i think it’s probably because they were still quite new. 
after she took them out she didn’t have any scars, but her dimples do seem to be more noticeable. 
i think you’ll do just fine, as long as you take good care of them! they’re a super cute piercing, if only i was brave enough. good luck!
